questions.enonce_markdown:
Describe the role of the following devices during data transmission.

(a) Repeater.

(b) Multiplexer.

(c) Gateway. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Repeater (1 mark).** A repeater receives a signal that has become weak and distorted over a long cable (attenuation), **regenerates (amplifies and cleans) it** and sends it on, so that the signal can travel a longer distance or connect two segments of the same network.

**(b) Multiplexer (1 mark).** A multiplexer **combines several input signals (data streams) into one signal** that is sent over a single shared channel (cable, fibre or radio link); at the other end a demultiplexer separates them again. It saves cables and makes better use of the bandwidth of the link.

**(c) Gateway (1 mark).** A gateway **connects two networks that use different protocols or architectures** and **translates** the data and addresses from one protocol to the other; it is also the point through which a local network is connected to other networks such as the Internet (for example the default gateway or a mail gateway).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Draw a well labeled diagram to show the different components in any data communication system. (4 marks)

(b) Give **two** main reasons why most organisations prefer client-server networks to peer-to-peer networks. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Components of a data communication system (4 marks)**

A data communication system has five components: the **message** (the data to be sent: text, numbers, images, audio, video), the **sender** (source device), the **transmission medium** (the path: cable, fibre, radio waves), the **receiver** (destination device) and the **protocol** (the rules agreed by sender and receiver to communicate).

```text
              PROTOCOL (rules agreed by the sender and the receiver)
        +----------------------------------------------------------------+
        |                                                                |
        v                                                                v
  +------------+      MESSAGE       +--------------------+    MESSAGE  +------------+
  |   SENDER   | -----------------> | TRANSMISSION MEDIUM| -----------> |  RECEIVER  |
  |  (source)  |   (data, signal)   | (cable, fibre,     |              | (destination)
  +------------+                    |  radio waves)      |              +------------+
                                    +--------------------+
                                              ^
                                              | noise / interference
```

(Marks are given for the five labelled components and for the direction of the flow of the message from the sender to the receiver.)

**(b) Two reasons for preferring client-server networks (4 marks, 2 marks each)**

Any two of:

1. **Centralised administration and security.** Users, passwords, permissions, software updates and **backups** are managed from the server in one place; in a peer-to-peer network each computer is managed separately and the security is weaker.
2. **Better performance with many users.** Resources (files, printers, databases) are held on a powerful dedicated server that is built to serve many clients at the same time, so access stays fast; peer computers slow down when many users share one ordinary computer.
3. **Scalability and reliability.** New clients can be added easily without reorganising the network, and the data kept on the server can be protected with redundancy (RAID, regular backup); a peer-to-peer network becomes difficult to manage beyond about ten computers.
4. **Central control of shared data.** All users work on the same up-to-date copy of the data, which is kept consistent and can be monitored.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The principal of a school decides to connect the school's local area network to the Internet and then set up a Wi-Fi connection in order to allow wireless access to the Internet for teachers on campus.

(a) Identify **three** devices that will be required to support these changes. (3 marks)

(b) On a specific day, the Wi-Fi transmission is significantly slower than on previous days. Describe **three** factors that could have caused this degradation in transmission speed. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Three devices required (3 marks, 1 mark each)**

1. **Modem** (or the equipment supplied by the Internet service provider): links the school to the ISP line and converts the signals for transmission over it.
2. **Router:** connects the school LAN to the Internet, directs the packets between the two networks (and usually provides the firewall and gives out IP addresses by DHCP).
3. **Wireless access point (WAP):** connects the Wi-Fi devices to the wired network by radio, creating the wireless network for the teachers.

Other acceptable answers: a switch (to connect the access point and the router to the LAN), a firewall, and wireless network interface cards (Wi-Fi adapters) in the teachers' computers if they have none.

**(b) Three factors that could slow the Wi-Fi (3 marks, 1 mark each)**

Any three of:

- **Too many users** connected at the same time, or heavy use (downloads, video streaming): the bandwidth is shared and the network is congested.
- **Distance from the access point and obstacles** (thick walls, metal, furniture): the signal is attenuated and weaker.
- **Interference** from other wireless devices on the same channel or frequency (neighbouring Wi-Fi networks, microwave ovens, Bluetooth devices, cordless phones).
- **Unauthorised users** who have found the Wi-Fi password and use the connection, or **malware** that sends large amounts of data.
- **A problem at the Internet service provider** (a slow or congested link) or old, faulty equipment or an outdated Wi-Fi standard.
